PullRequest.Title: Agents: no traffic-light inset in fullscreen auxiliary windows
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes the Agents window title bar on macOS reserving the traffic-light inset in an auxiliary window that is in native full screen.

The title bar checked fullscreen of the main window and the inset CSS depended on `.monaco-workbench.fullscreen`, which only the main container gets. The part now tracks fullscreen of its own window and sets a `titlebar-fullscreen` class on itself, which drives the inset. Main window behavior is unchanged.

How to test: on macOS, open an auxiliary (chat or editor) window in the Agents window, enter native full screen; the title should sit flush left.

Validation: `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/titlebarPart.test.ts` (33 passing; new test fails without the fix), eslint on changed files clean.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create the main Agents titlebar during workbench startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: TitlebarPart.createContentArea now resolves the owning window, reads fullscreen state from an in-memory map, and toggles one class before constructing the existing titlebar DOM. This constant local work is on startup's UI-thread critical path; no new asynchronous work must complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one main titlebar; the added state read and class mutation are O(1).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous and serialized on the renderer UI thread; no queue, fan-out, or concurrent resource creation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fullscreen state is an O(1) Map lookup keyed by window ID. There is no cold-cache fill, negative cache, or retry behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed lines and create lifecycle show one map read and one DOM class toggle per titlebar creation, with no layout read after the write.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style-recalculation duration is not measured, but the mutation is a single startup-only class toggle on a small titlebar subtree.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds only bounded local startup work and does not force synchronous layout or cross an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and later dispose an auxiliary editor/chat window with an Agents titlebar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each auxiliary titlebar performs the same O(1) owning-window lookup, fullscreen map read, class toggle, and listener registration during local DOM construction. Electron's existing fullscreen-state query is fired asynchronously by NativeAuxiliaryWindow and is not awaited by titlebar creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the native host for the new auxiliary window's initial fullscreen state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One asynchronous query per Electron auxiliary window construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one-per-window native fullscreen query already ran before this PR; the changed titlebar code only consumes the existing local event/state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The constructor invokes the async method without awaiting it, so the query is off titlebar creation's critical path; its result may later update local fullscreen state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One added listener and one initial class toggle per live auxiliary window; cumulative state scales linearly with the number of open auxiliary windows, while creation cost remains O(1) per window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Titlebars are constructed synchronously per window. Existing native fullscreen IPC queries can overlap when multiple windows open, but the diff neither adds nor increases those queries. Fullscreen listeners are disposed through the part's Disposable lifecycle.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each window has one fullscreen value in the existing in-memory map; there is no new cache or repeated miss path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: TitleService creates one part per auxiliary container, the changed listener is registered in that part's disposable store, and disposal tears it down.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The maximum number of simultaneously open auxiliary windows is user-dependent, but each window already owns a full workbench surface and the added retained state is one callback plus captured references.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: lifecycle cleanup is present, no expensive boundary was introduced, and per-window CPU/memory overhead is small and bounded by live windows.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enter or leave fullscreen in the main or an auxiliary window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing fullscreen signal updates WindowManager and synchronously emits to listeners. The new listener compares the event window ID and only the matching titlebar toggles one class; on macOS custom titlebars the existing spacer listener also performs its prior style update. Writes are not followed by geometry reads, so layout can be deferred to the browser render phase.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive the existing Electron main-window enter/leave-fullscreen notification and update renderer-local fullscreen state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One incoming notification per actual main-window fullscreen state transition; duplicate state assignments are suppressed by WindowManager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Electron fullscreen notification and WindowManager event were handled before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The notification precedes local listener dispatch; the PR adds only a local class toggle after receipt and no request/response IPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive the existing host-service fullscreen event for the affected registered window and update renderer-local fullscreen state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One host event per actual affected-window transition; listeners filter by target window ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The host fullscreen event already updated WindowManager before this PR; titlebars previously used main-window state for spacer handling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing event is the source of the local state change. The PR does not add an IPC call or move an IPC query onto this path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Event dispatch visits one newly added listener per live titlebar (O(W) ID comparisons), but exactly one titlebar performs the added DOM class mutation for the target window. Fullscreen transitions are low-frequency user/window events rather than frame, resize, scroll, or input-loop work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fullscreen callbacks run synchronously and serially in the renderer. There is no burst, Promise fan-out, limiter, or queued repeated work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The target titlebar reads the already-updated O(1) fullscreen map entry. No invalidation, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the global emitter, ID filter, map lookup, class toggle, CSS selector, and disposable ownership are directly visible in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style-recalculation cost varies by browser and titlebar contents, but only one small subtree is invalidated per rare transition and there is no forced-layout evidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: although global dispatch adds O(W) trivial comparisons, only the target incurs one required DOM write, listeners are cleaned up, and the low-frequency path has no forced layout or new boundary work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and traced titlebar startup, auxiliary-window lifecycle, and fullscreen transitions. The PR adds bounded in-memory state reads, disposable listeners, and one target-scoped class mutation; it introduces no expensive boundary, hot-loop work, forced layout, unbounded retention, or actionable performance regression.
